headings.reviewNote: Prohibits new surface coal mining after September 28, 1979 (subject to valid existing rights) on specified federal lands, near parks/historic sites without joint approval, within one hundred feet of public roads or cemeteries, and within three hundred feet of occupied dwellings (unless waived) or public buildings.

entries.reviewSummary: Drafted 4 subsection headings for 444.890 governing unsuitability planning criteria, citizen petition hearings, impact statements, and mandatory buffer zones around parks, roads, and occupied buildings.

headings.title: Application for review of notice or order
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes permittees and affected persons to apply for review of cessation orders or notices within thirty days of receipt.

headings.title: Investigation findings and written commission decision
headings.reviewNote: Directs investigation, hearing, and written findings vacating, modifying, or affirming orders within thirty days.

headings.title: Temporary relief from orders and decision standards
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes temporary relief within five days for cessation orders upon showing success likelihood and no harm.

headings.title: Show-cause hearing and permit suspension or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Governs show-cause hearings and requires written decisions within sixty days concerning permit suspension or revocation.

headings.title: Assessment of costs and attorney fees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes assessing reasonable costs, expenses, and attorney fees incurred in administrative enforcement proceedings.

headings.title: Hearing officer designation and five-day temporary relief decisions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the chairman to designate a commission member or Missouri Bar member as hearing officer to recommend decisions to the commission, except the hearing officer makes the decision in five-day temporary relief hearings.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 444.895 governing administrative review of cessation orders and notices, written decisions, temporary relief, show-cause hearings, cost/fee assessments, and hearing officers.

headings.title: Severability of statutory provisions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the invalidity of any provision of this law shall not affect the remaining statutory provisions.

headings.title: Preservation of water resource enforcement rights
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this law affects any person's right under applicable law to enforce or protect interests in water resources affected by surface coal mining.

headings.title: Replacement of damaged water supplies
headings.reviewNote: Requires surface coal mine operators to replace underground or surface water supplies used for domestic, agricultural, industrial, or other legitimate purposes that are contaminated, diminished, or interrupted by mining.

headings.title: Blaster training, examination, and certification regulations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to promulgate regulations requiring training, examination, and certification of persons engaging in or directly responsible for blasting or explosives in surface coal mining.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 444.905 governing severability, preserved water-resource rights, replacement of damaged water supplies, and blaster certification regulations.

headings.title: Authorized uses of abandoned mine reclamation fund
headings.reviewNote: Lists seven permitted uses including reclaiming past coal-mined lands and waters, sealing voids under section 444.935, land acquisition, studies and demonstration projects, emergencies, and administrative expenses.

headings.title: Five-tier priority order for fund expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Establishes five mandatory expenditure priorities in order: extreme-danger protection, general public health/safety protection, environmental restoration, public facility repair/enhancement, and public-land development.

headings.title: Eligible lands and waters for reclamation expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Defines eligible lands and waters lacking continuing reclamation responsibility: pre-September 28, 1979 abandoned sites, August 4, 1977–November 21, 1980 underbonded sites, and August 4, 1977–October 1, 1991 insolvent-surety sites.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 444.915 governing authorized uses of the Abandoned Mine Reclamation Fund, five-tier expenditure priorities, and eligible lands and waters.

headings.title: Police-power entry for reclamation after findings and notice
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes entry for reclamation upon four commission findings and mailed or posted/published notice as a police-power exercise (not condemnation or trespass), offsetting owner damage claims by work costs and benefits.

headings.title: Right of entry for studies and exploratory work
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes commission staff, agents, and contractors to enter any property as a police-power exercise to conduct studies or exploratory work determining adverse mining effects and reclamation feasibility.

headings.title: Acquisition of adversely affected land by state
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes acquiring adversely affected land by purchase, donation, or condemnation when necessary for successful reclamation under three specified public-use, facility, or emergency conditions.

headings.title: State title and market-value purchase price
headings.reviewNote: Vests title to acquired lands in the state and requires purchase prices to reflect market value as adversely affected by past coal mining.

headings.title: Competitive public sale of suitable reclaimed land
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes selling acquired land suitable for industrial, commercial, residential, or recreational development by competitive bidding at not less than fair market value consistent with land use plans.

headings.title: Local public hearing on post-reclamation use or disposition
headings.reviewNote: Requires holding a local public hearing when requested after public notice to allow citizens and local governments maximum participation in post-reclamation use or disposition decisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 444.925 governing entry for reclamation and exploratory studies, land acquisition, state title and market-value pricing, competitive public sales, and disposition hearings; source note records original-rolls word discrepancy ('of') in subsection 6.

headings.title: Filing reclamation lien, appraisal cap, and pre-1977 exemption
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes filing an itemized expenditure statement and independent pre-reclamation appraisal in the county recorder's office within six months, capped at appraised value increase and exempting non-consenting surface owners prior to May 2, 1977.

headings.title: Sixty-day commission hearing on value increase and appeal
headings.reviewNote: Allows the landowner sixty days from lien filing to request a commission hearing determining the market-value increase, recorded as the lien amount and appealable as provided by law.

headings.title: Recorder entry, effective date, and second-only lien priority
headings.reviewNote: Requires entering the lien in the county recorder of deeds office, making it effective as of the expenditure date with priority second only to real estate taxes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 444.930 governing abandoned-mine reclamation liens, market-value caps and pre-May 2, 1977 owner exemptions, commission valuation hearings, and lien priority.

headings.title: Annual report on abandoned mine reclamation fund
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual commission reports starting not later than January 1, 1981 to Congress and the general assembly on abandoned mine reclamation fund operations and future-use recommendations.

headings.title: General powers and rulemaking to administer fund
headings.reviewNote: Grants the commission power to engage in any work and do all things necessary or expedient, including promulgating rules, to implement and administer the abandoned mine reclamation fund.

headings.title: Cooperative projects with federal and state agencies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to engage in cooperative projects with federal agencies and any state or its governmental agencies to administer the fund.

headings.title: Attorney general injunctions against interference with entry
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes requesting the attorney general to bring an equity action for an injunction restraining interference with right of entry or work under sections 444.915 to 444.940.

headings.title: Construction and operation of mine-drainage treatment plants
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes constructing and operating water pollution control and treatment plants (including major interceptors) for mine drainage meeting at least Federal Water Pollution Control Act standards.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 444.940 governing annual abandoned mine fund reports to Congress and the general assembly, general powers and rulemaking, cooperative projects, entry injunctions, and mine-drainage treatment plants.

headings.title: Phase I bond minimums, open-pit rule, and annual adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing a Phase I reclamation bond of at least two thousand five hundred dollars per acre (ten thousand dollars for coal prep areas) with annual rulemaking adjustment caps and a ten-thousand-dollar minimum (or twenty-acre equivalent per open-pit acre under one thousand bonded acres).

headings.title: Rulemaking effectiveness pursuant to section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no rule or portion of a rule promulgated under chapter 444 becomes effective unless promulgated pursuant to section 536.024.

headings.title: Corporate surety execution and collateral deposit alternatives
headings.reviewNote: Requires execution by operator and licensed corporate surety, or permits depositing cash, irrevocable letters of credit, U.S. or Missouri negotiable bonds, or negotiable certificates of deposit.

headings.title: Self-bonding without surety and alternative bonding systems
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes accepting an applicant's self-bond upon showing a service agent and financial solvency, or adopting an alternative bonding system consistent with P.L. 95-87.

headings.title: Bond liability duration, Phase I release, and forfeiture availability
headings.reviewNote: Continues Phase I bond liability until Phase I completion (allowing release of at least eighty percent, retaining the rest until Phase III release) and makes the full bond available for all reclamation phases upon forfeiture.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 444.950 governing Phase I reclamation bond amounts and adjustments, section 536.024 rulemaking, surety/collateral options, self-bonding or alternative systems, and bond liability/release; source note records original-rolls discrepancy ('Subsection 9') in subsection 4.

headings.title: Creation of coal mine land reclamation fund
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Coal Mine Land Reclamation Fund for section 444.965 assessments and section 444.970 penalties, used to complete reclamation after performance bond proceeds are exhausted.

headings.title: State treasurer investment and interest credit to fund
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state treasurer to deposit unneeded fund moneys in interest-bearing accounts and credit earned interest to the fund.

headings.title: Fund accumulation ceiling and equitable excess distribution
headings.reviewNote: Allows the fund to accumulate to the greater of seven million dollars or two thousand five hundred dollars per unreleased mined acre, equitably distributing excess to contributing companies.

headings.title: Nonreversion of fund balances to general revenue
headings.reviewNote: Protects fund balances from lapsing into general revenue at the end of state fiscal years.

headings.title: Forty-sixty allocation for pre- and post-1988 revoked permits
headings.reviewNote: Allocates forty percent of post-September 1, 1988 assessments (plus prior balance) to pre-September 1, 1988 revoked permits and sixty percent to post-September 1, 1988 revoked permits, shifting all assessments to the sixty-percent pool once the forty-percent pool is sufficient.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 444.960 establishing the Coal Mine Land Reclamation Fund, state treasurer investment, accumulation ceiling and excess distribution, non-lapse status, and 40%/60% assessment allocation.

headings.title: Mandatory tonnage assessment on Phase I permittees
headings.reviewNote: Requires every permittee filing a section 444.950 Phase I bond beginning September 1, 1988 to pay an additional assessment to the commission for the coal mine land reclamation fund.

headings.title: Monthly assessment payment and rate schedule
headings.reviewNote: Establishes monthly assessments of forty-five cents per ton on the first fifty thousand tons and thirty cents on the next fifty thousand.

headings.title: Suspension and resumption at seven-million-dollar threshold
headings.reviewNote: Suspends assessments when the fiscal year-end balance exceeds seven million dollars (except requiring new permittees to pay until matching comparable existing permittees) and resumes assessments when below seven million dollars.

headings.title: Resumption rates after forty-percent pool accumulation
headings.reviewNote: Sets resumed assessment rates at twenty-five cents and fifteen cents per ton after older revoked sites are funded.

headings.title: Emergency rate increase below two-million-dollar threshold
headings.reviewNote: Increases assessment rates after September 1, 1998 to thirty and twenty cents per ton whenever the fund falls below two million dollars until reaching at least three million dollars at fiscal year-end, then reverting to subsection 4 rates.

entries.reviewSummary: Drafted 5 subsection headings for 444.965 establishing Phase I tonnage assessments, monthly rate schedules, balance suspension thresholds, resumption rates, and emergency rate adjustments.

headings.title: Late penalty for delinquent assessment payments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a penalty of twenty-five cents per ton for assessment payments delinquent more than thirty days and prepayment orders.

headings.title: Operating prohibition for uncompleted reclamation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits operating in Missouri until full costs of state-completed reclamation are reimbursed and authorizes recovery suits.

headings.title: Tonnage penalty for delinquent reclamation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a penalty of twenty-five cents per ton and supplemental bonding for substantial delinquency in completing reclamation.

headings.title: No state obligation for general revenue reclamation
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the general assembly is under no obligation to appropriate general revenue moneys to reclaim mined land.
